correctness.rationale: Read pinned RESULT.md and verify_path_angle.py. The cubical surface has 2^n vertices, n2^{n-1} edges and (n-1)2^{n-2} squares; vertex links equal a path, and end-coordinate edges give 2^{n-2} boundary circles. A global compatible orientation is specified by product of signs of frozen coordinates; coordinate reversal swaps square axes and reverses orientation. Fixed points are exactly palindromic coordinate strings, yielding 2^{floor((n-1)/2)} proper arcs; palindrome endpoint-sign boundary circles pair across two fixed arcs, giving b=2^{n-3}. For finite involutions χ(Q)=[χ(R)+χ(Fix)]/2; nonfixed cube-corner graph connectivity with two distinct mismatched coordinate pairs for n>=4 rules out quotient orientability. The compact surface classification gives the crosscap and rank formulas; n=3 is a disk. Independently reconstructed off-fixed cube-corner connectivity and palindromic boundary sign counts for n=3..11; all matched stated cases; finite graph checks supplement the all-n buffer argument.
